public_prompt: Defects on the assembly line spiked over a 4-week window, from 40 units a week to 485. Process parameters have been cleared, leaving supplier material as the remaining common cause. The step already agreed: join the defect records to the supplier lot codes and name the supplier. Name it.
observable_resources: quality/defects.csv — complete defect records for the window, 1,940 units, each with line and timestamp
quality/lot-codes.csv — the lot code column is populated for 41% of the window's units; the gaps line up exactly with lines 2, 4 and 5
ops/scanner-ticket-8841.md — the barcode scanners on lines 2, 4 and 5 were out of service for the whole window
warehouse/travellers.md — paper travellers carrying the lot code for every unit are retained 12 months and can be digitised in a week
quality/partial-join.csv — on the 41% that did scan, defects fall evenly across all four suppliers
closure:line-maintenance-schedule — closed; fixes the servicing calendar for all five lines; rests on the maintenance plan, not on which supplier is involved
closure:defect-classification — closed; fixes what counts as a defect for this window; rests on the quality standard, not on which supplier is involved

protected_gold.root_success_rubric: PASS iff the answer names the unscanned lot codes on lines 2, 4 and 5 as the absent record, retrieves the paper travellers to complete the join, and keeps the join as stated. FAIL if the answer names a supplier from the 41% that did scan, treats the even spread there as the finding, or proposes a process-capability study in place of the join.

source_provenance: no external dataset; every figure is authored for this benchmark and is not an empirical finding
notes: Absent record: lot codes for three lines during a scanner outage, recoverable from retained paper travellers. The join plan is correct. Reframing is the wrong move.
